Introduction
Background
Students who arrive at their classrooms are often unaware whether the room has already been unlocked, forcing them to wait outside, sometimes for a long time, until personnel arrive to open the door.
Both situations create recurring problems that affect the daily campus experience, including:
Lost instructional and consultation time
Repeated, unnecessary trips to the faculty office
Frustration, anxiety, and helplessness among students and faculty
Between the two problems, classroom door delays have been identified as the more frequent issue, since they affect students at the start of nearly every class period.

The current process is entirely manual. Students either wait outside the locked room or walk to the faculty office to look for personnel with the keys, with no way to check status remotely. Likewise, students visiting the faculty office have no way to confirm a professor's availability aside from physically checking, often finding out only after arriving that the professor is out, in a meeting, or already occupied.

This lack of real-time information forces students to rely on guesswork, hallway conversations, or repeated failed visits, resulting in wasted time and unnecessary stress for both students and faculty.
Objectives

The objective of DoorSync is to give students real-time visibility into classroom unlock status and professor availability, replacing guesswork and unnecessary waiting with a clear, reliable source of information.

The system aims to reduce the time students spend waiting outside locked classrooms by letting faculty flag a room for opening and notifying personnel, while letting professors set their own availability status within the app.
In addition, the solution is expected to reduce unnecessary trips to the faculty office and improve coordination among students, professors, and personnel across campus.

Assumptions

DoorSync assumes that students, professors, and personnel have access to a smartphone or computer with internet connectivity. It is assumed that professors will update their status when leaving or returning to the faculty office, and that personnel will act on unlock requests within a reasonable timeframe. Specific business rules, exception handling, and system behavior are still to be defined as development progresses.

The app provides three distinct views, Student, Professor, and Personnel, accessed through a tab switcher, each showing only the information and actions relevant to that role.
Status badges are color-coded for quick recognition: blue indicates Available or Unlocked, while yellow indicates Occupied or Locked.

1. Professor identifies a classroom that needs to be unlocked (e.g., before a scheduled class).
2. Professor opens the DoorSync app and selects the room from the room list.

1. Professor taps “Notify personnel.”
2. The app displays a confirmation toast: “Request sent to personnel — awaiting unlock.”

1. The system creates an Unlock Request record, timestamps it, and keeps Room Status = Locked.
2. The system routes the request to the on-duty Personnel account(s).
3. If the request is not resolved within a reasonable timeframe, it is flagged and escalated — to be determined once the system design and development are finalized.

1. Personnel receives a notification of the new Unlock Request (shown as a pulsing Locked badge with requester and time flagged, e.g., “Flagged by Prof. M. Santos · 2 min ago”).
2. Personnel proceeds to the flagged room and physically unlocks the door.
3. Personnel taps “Mark unlocked” in the app to close out the request.

1. The system updates Room Status from Locked to Unlocked.
2. The system sends a status-change notification to students tracking that room.
3. The completed request moves to the Personnel “Completed today” list.

1. Student views “Your next classes” in the app, showing each room with a Locked (red, pulsing) or Unlocked (green) badge.
2. Once Room Status changes to Unlocked, the student proceeds to the classroom.

1. Professor opens the app's status panel.
2. Professor taps the Available / Occupied toggle to set status.

1. The system updates the Professor Status in real time.
2. The system logs the change to the professor's “Recent activity” feed (e.g., “You set status to Occupied · 8:55 AM”).
3. Whether a push notification is sent on every change, or only in specific cases, is to be determined once the system design and development are finalized.

Design Process: Following the 10-step process (Casalla, Software Design — Database Design Workshop)

A professor sets their own availability. A professor flags a room that needs unlocking; personnel acts on the request and unlocks it. Students check room and professor status, and can subscribe to be notified when a specific room or professor's status changes.
Room status, professor status, unlock requests (who flagged, who resolved, when), and which students are subscribed to which rooms/professors for notifications.
Checks room/professor status and can subscribe to status-change alerts.
Sets their own Available/Occupied status; flags rooms that need unlocking.
Receives unlock requests and marks rooms as unlocked.
A classroom with a Locked/Unlocked status.
One flagged request — connects a professor, a room, and the personnel who resolves it.
See each table's own sheet for the full attribute list and primary key. IDs use a readable prefix format (e.g. STU-001, PROF-001, RM-201) — simple to read and guaranteed unique.
PERSONNEL (1) — resolves — (0..*) UNLOCKREQUEST  (Personnel is optional/blank until assigned)
A student can subscribe to alerts for many rooms, and a room can have many student subscribers. Resolved with junction table ROOM_SUBSCRIPTION (composite key: StudentID + RoomID).
A student can subscribe to many professors, and a professor can have many student subscribers. Resolved with junction table PROFESSOR_SUBSCRIPTION (composite key: StudentID + ProfessorID).

A professor can flag many different rooms over time, and a room can be flagged by many different professors over time. Resolved by UNLOCKREQUEST, which also carries its own identity (RequestID) and a third relationship to PERSONNEL — the same pattern as an APPOINTMENT connecting a patient and doctor while also recording who handled it.
Professor and room names/emails/buildings are stored once, in PROFESSOR and ROOM, and referenced by ID everywhere else — never copied into UNLOCKREQUEST or the subscription tables.
CurrentStatus lives only on PROFESSOR and ROOM (the entity it describes), not duplicated onto UNLOCKREQUEST rows.
Each table describes exactly one kind of thing, and every non-key column depends only on that table's primary key.
STUDENT — see its own tab for schema and sample data.
PROFESSOR — see its own tab for schema and sample data.

ROOM_SUBSCRIPTION — see its own tab for schema and sample data.
PROFESSOR_SUBSCRIPTION — see its own tab for schema and sample data.
Every primary key column has conditional formatting that turns a row red if that ID (or ID combination, for the two junction tables) is duplicated elsewhere in the same column.
Status columns (CurrentStatus, Status) are dropdown lists, so only the allowed values can be entered.
Foreign key columns (RoomID, ProfessorID, PersonnelID, StudentID) are dropdown lists sourced directly from the referenced table's ID column, so a typo'd or non-existent ID can't be entered.
